clue.text: Measure of brightness in girl — a top model?

indicators.note: the measure of brightness is placed in the girl's name, which is split around it

parts.note: Dee is a girl's name
the lux is the SI unit of illuminance

explanation.surface: A young woman's glowing looks suggest she might be a leading fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-of-the-range model of a car or gadget is the luxury version, the de luxe one.

clue.text: Before dance, I chatted, given stare

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the dance in the answer
chatted signals the pronoun is heard spoken, so it is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Before a dance someone talked and then stared.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to look hard at them.

clue.text: One needs pluck in this country's university, and double the French

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, this country for a British paper

indicators.note: double means the French article is written twice

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone needs courage at a British university, twice over in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukulele is a small guitar whose strings are plucked.

clue.text: Sea creature to shun ice formation

indicators.note: formation tells us these letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sea animal avoids forming ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinus is the genus of sea urchins.

clue.text: Islander's oral lessons I am able to follow

indicators.note: oral signals that the word for lessons is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a course is a series of lessons
can means am able

explanation.surface: Someone from an island has spoken lessons and claims to be capable of keeping up.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works only in non-rhotic British speech, where the R of the word for lessons is silent; 'to follow' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Corsica, the French island in the Mediterranean, is a Corsican islander.

clue.text: Unconventional, one leaves position over rent fiasco

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
the numeral departs from the word for position

parts.note: an office is a position or post
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a fiasco is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An eccentric quits their job over a disastrous rent dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFICE less I gives OFFCE; 'fiasco' turns RENT into NTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-centre is an idiom for eccentric or slightly odd.

clue.text: Always, in time, admit what makes sense

indicators.note: the word for always goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a season is a period of time
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Sooner or later you must accept what is sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept logic is the idiom for coming round to the sensible view.

clue.text: Make alterations to 'suits and come to dance

indicators.note: dance means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tailor makes alterations to suits, and people come for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To customise is to modify something to suit one's taste.

clue.text: Muses, then scrapes enough for half a round?

parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth
a hole is a scrape or predicament

explanation.surface: Someone thinks, then scratches together enough to cover half a round.
explanation.walkthrough: A round of golf is eighteen holes, so half a round is nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of a standard golf round is the front or back nine.

clue.text: Country girl shortly leaves study

indicators.note: the girl departs from the study, so her letters are taken out of it

parts.note: a perusal is a careful reading or study
Sal is a shortened form of the girl's name Sally

explanation.surface: A country lass briefly abandons her studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' wants to be read together; 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a nation in South America.

clue.text: Beer sailor found in hold

parts.note: a half is a half-pint of beer in a British pub
Admiral Nelson is Britain's most famous sailor

explanation.surface: A pint-drinking sailor is discovered in the ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' suggests a ship's cargo space; it is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wrestling grip in which an arm is locked behind the opponent's neck.

clue.text: Lose willpower I've developed, being shut in prison

indicators.note: the reworked letters are enclosed within the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: developed signals the letters of the short word are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's resolve has grown while locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose willpower' is the definition: to give in. 'developed' signals the anagram of the contracted word, VEI, held in the slang for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in or collapse under pressure is to stop resisting, an idiom for losing resolve.

clue.text: Giant live male insect

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
he is the male pronoun
a moth is a winged insect

explanation.surface: A huge living male bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical beast's name is used for anything monstrously large.

clue.text: Trees burning in town occupied by soldiers?

parts.note: alders are trees of the birch family
burning means very hot

explanation.surface: Trees are ablaze in a garrison town.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDERSHOT is a Hampshire town, home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This town has long been the main garrison base of the British Army.

clue.text: Woman with arm around husband in case of a fall

parts.note: Ava is a woman's name

indicators.note: the weapon goes around the abbreviation for husband

parts.note: a lance is a weapon, an arm

explanation.surface: A wife with her arm round her husband to catch him if he trips.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a fall of snow, one instance of a fall.

clue.text: Remove leaves from tea and do life breakdown

indicators.note: a breakdown breaks the letters up and rebuilds them in a new order

explanation.surface: Strip leaves from tea and suffer a life breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To defoliate is to strip a plant of its foliage.

clue.text: For the record, it's ensuring marketability

definitions.text: For the record, it's ensuring marketability

parts.words: For the record, it's ensuring marketability
parts.note: reads like a formal statement about sales, but describes putting a record on sale

explanation.surface: Officially, a firm is making sure its product can be sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Issuing a record puts it on the market for sale.

clue.text: Very good evidence of drugs at school

parts.note: being high is a sign of drug use
a class is a group in a school

explanation.surface: Proof of drug use in a school.
explanation.definitionFit: High-class means of superior quality.

clue.text: Sort of medication given after first serious accident

indicators.note: the medication follows the first letter in the answer
the opening letter of the word serious is taken

parts.note: a pill is a form of medication

explanation.surface: A patient is given a tablet after a bad accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill is a fall or tumble, a minor accident.

clue.text: Terrible flaw in organisation allows in United's first.

indicators.note: the rearranged letters admit another letter into their midst
being put into organisation means the letters are reordered
the opening letter of United is taken

explanation.surface: A dreadful weakness in a football club's management lets their opponents in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in organisation' turns FLAW into AWFL, and U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and terrible are synonyms for very bad.

clue.text: They could be paid to go on a course

definitions.text: They could be paid to go on a course

parts.words: They could be paid to go on a course
parts.note: reads like fees for an educational course, but the course is a golf course and the charge is for playing it

explanation.surface: Tuition fees might be paid to attend a training course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs charge visitors a fee to play their course.

clue.text: Serious listener's cosy home

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: Someone who listens takes their snug home seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intent.

clue.text: Journey to the unknown, perhaps rather impetuous?

parts.note: a flight is a journey by air
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Is flying off to an unknown place a little rash?
explanation.definitionFit: Flighty describes someone fickle and capricious, a near synonym.

clue.text: Tide has turned — no one raised the issue

indicators.note: turned means the letters of tide are rearranged
in a down clue raised means the letters read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: With the tide turned, nobody brought up the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has turned' makes EDIT from TIDE; 'raised' turns NO I upwards into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue of a newspaper or book.

clue.text: Daughter's forsaking casual affair for marriage

indicators.note: the daughter abandons the affair, so her letter is taken out of it

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual romantic affair

explanation.surface: A daughter gives up a fling in order to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union, including one by wedlock between families.

clue.text: Cultivating endless fruit that's been processed

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: raising crops is cultivating them

explanation.surface: Growing fruit without end that goes on to be processed.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a grape that has been dried.

clue.text: Generous fish one placed by slab

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
I is the Roman numeral one
a table is a flat slab

explanation.surface: A big-hearted fishmonger lays a fish on a slab.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable and generous both describe giving freely.

clue.text: Salute flag

definitions.meaning: to flag down a taxi is to signal to it

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers greeting someone and signalling a passing cab.

clue.text: Give power to work unit — one seen shuffling around

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the other pieces
shuffling means the letters of seen are mixed up

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An electrician powers up a work station, watched by someone wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one seen' looks like one piece of fodder, but 'one' is the numeral; only 'seen' is shuffled (ENSE) to wrap the physics unit and the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to supply with energy or vigour.

clue.text: Putting into dock is particularly awkward

definitions.meaning: putting someone in the dock means hearing their case in court
difficult and annoying to deal with

explanation.definitionFit: Hearing a case in court and being exasperating share the one word.
